item.research_question: Can a high entropy alloy nanocatalyst enable ambient hydrogenation of solid aromatics?
item.processing_route: solvothermal method with acetylacetone salts as metal precursors
key_findings: 100% hydrogenation of carbon-carbon unsaturated bonds in solid 1,4-bis(phenylethynyl)benzene (DEB)
Threefold higher hydrogen uptake for DEB-contained composites compared to conventional Pd catalysts
Nearly 100% reactivity for ambient hydrogenation of a broad range of aromatics
PdPtRu alloying is crucial for hydrogenating phenyl groups
All five elements work synergistically to regulate the reaction rate
item.mechanism: The PdPtRuCuNi HEA catalyst activates H2 and DEB molecules, allowing for the hydrogenation of alkynyl and phenyl groups
item.future_work: Large-scale preparation of PdPtRu-containing HEA nanocatalysts and exploration of catalytic hydrogenation for different functional groups
quotes: Ambient hydrogenation of solid aromatics enabled by a high entropy alloy nanocatalyst
100% hydrogenation of carbon-carbon unsaturated bonds, including alkynyl and phenyl groups, in solid 1,4-bis(phenylethynyl)benzene (DEB) at 25 °C under ≤1 bar H2 and solventless condition
PdPtRu alloying is critical for hydrogenating phenyl groups, with all elements collectively regulating the hydrogenation reaction rate

records.text: Paper card. Question: Can a high entropy alloy nanocatalyst enable ambient hydrogenation of solid aromatics?. System: PdPtRuCuNi high entropy alloy (HEA) nanocatalyst. Processing: solvothermal method with acetylacetone salts as metal precursors. Test conditions: 25 °C, ≤1 bar H2, solventless condition. Findings: 100% hydrogenation of carbon-carbon unsaturated bonds in solid 1,4-bis(phenylethynyl)benzene (DEB); Threefold higher hydrogen uptake for DEB-contained composites compared to conventional Pd catalysts; Nearly 100% reactivity for ambient hydrogenation of a broad range of aromatics; PdPtRu alloying is crucial for hydrogenating phenyl groups; All five elements work synergistically to regulate the reaction rate. Mechanism: The PdPtRuCuNi HEA catalyst activates H2 and DEB molecules, allowing for the hydrogenation of alkynyl and phenyl groups. Future work: Large-scale preparation of PdPtRu-containing HEA nanocatalysts and exploration of catalytic hydrogenation for different functional groups. Quote: "Ambient hydrogenation of solid aromatics enabled by a high entropy alloy nanocatalyst"
